data.narrative:
Transmutex is a Series A nuclear energy company that has raised $23M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comparable universe of 11 companies across the nuclear sector—three public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and eight private firms including Fuse Energy, Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, and General Matter.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier from the $23M total capital raised as a valuation proxy, yielding $46M. This reflects typical venture scaling mechanics at the Series A-to-next-round transition. Peer-median triangulation is not applicable: while four same-sector comparables exist, none satisfy minimum thresholds for same-stage or adjacent-stage clustering (fewer than three datapoints in each filtered cohort), making any narrow peer multiple unreliable without introducing sector-wide distortion.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $39M to $53M, with a median of $46M. This range reflects moderate confidence in the stage-progression methodology but acknowledges material uncertainty around nuclear subsector-specific growth rates, regulatory pathway timelines, and technology risk—factors not captured by venture-stage mechanics alone. A single quantitative method underpins the range; validation through additional peer clustering or revenue-based approaches would strengthen conviction, pending disclosure of comparable financials or narrower peer identification.
